newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet approves state firm's pipeline plans.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet approves state firm's pipeline plans.

text.p: The Thai government has approved 12 gas pipeline projects worth 78.05 billion baht ($312 million) by the state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand for construction during 1997-2005, an official said on Wednesday.
The projects are part of Thailand's pipeline masterplan.
They include major pipelines from the Thai-Malaysian Joint Development Area and a number of fields in the Gulf of Thailand, such as Pailin and Erawan.

Thailand's 8th National Economic and Social Development Plan (1997-2001) aims at sustaining imported energy at a level of not more than 70 percent of consumption and promote the procurement of local energy resources.
At present, 95 percent of indigenous natural gas procurement is from the Gulf of Thailand.
